description: Falsified Augmentin tablets lacking clavulanate entirely. Packaging closely mimics GSK branding. Identified by blurred holographic strip and incorrect font weight on batch number.

Substandard metformin tablets with dissolution failure — active ingredient does not dissolve properly in the body, leading to treatment failure in type 2 diabetes patients. Detected through post-market surveillance.
Falsified Coartem tablets detected with subtherapeutic artemether content (< 5% of declared amount). Packaging mimics genuine Novartis Coartem but contains incorrect active ingredients.

Counterfeit Viagra tablets widely circulating through online pharmacies and street vendors in Latin America. Products contain variable sildenafil doses (0–200mg) and undeclared substances including undeclared PDE5 inhibitors. Risk of severe hypotension.

Substandard paracetamol tablets with only 30–45% of stated active ingredient. Associated with treatment failure in fever management. Packaging uses correct typography but lacks regulatory approval marks required in ASEAN region.

Falsified amoxicillin capsules containing no active pharmaceutical ingredient. Packaging appears legitimate but lacks proper holographic security features. Batch numbers follow sequential pattern atypical of genuine manufacturers.

Unregistered amlodipine tablets circulating in conflict-affected regions. Products show variable potency (20–140% of stated dose). Associated with cases of uncontrolled hypertension and hypotensive episodes.

Falsified oxytocin injections detected. Product contains significantly reduced active ingredient. Risk of postpartum hemorrhage if used for obstetric indications. Packaging lacks mandatory cold-chain storage indicators.
Unregistered diazepam injections circulating through informal supply chains. Products show variable potency. Some contain undeclared benzodiazepines.

Falsified ciprofloxacin tablets with subtherapeutic content detected in West Africa. Associated with treatment failure in urinary tract and respiratory infections. Packaging lacks French language regulatory requirements.
Substandard cough syrups linked to acute kidney injury in children. Products contain diethylene glycol and ethylene glycol above acceptable limits. STOP USE IMMEDIATELY.

Counterfeit ivermectin tablets circulating globally during COVID-19 pandemic. Products range from veterinary ivermectin repurposed and repackaged to products with no active ingredient. Contains undeclared excipients.
Falsified hydroxychloroquine tablets containing zero active ingredient. Packaging closely mimics legitimate brands. Increased circulation observed during COVID-19 pandemic.

manufacturer: Various illegal manufacturers — primarily from Asia
description: Non-pharmacopoeial 225mg tramadol tablets circulating widely. Not approved in any jurisdiction — 225mg is not a recognized therapeutic dose. Associated with substance abuse and overdose deaths. No legitimate manufacturer produces this dose.

Falsified COVID-19 vaccines detected globally. Products may contain saline solution, distilled water, or other substances. Vials may have altered labels from real manufacturers including Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca.

Falsified azithromycin tablets with subtherapeutic content circulating in Southeast Asia. Associated with treatment failure in respiratory infections during COVID-19 pandemic. Some batches contain no active ingredient.
Falsified remdesivir injections detected during COVID-19 pandemic. Products contain subtherapeutic or zero active ingredient. Packaging mimics licensed generics.

Falsified human insulin vials detected in East Africa. Products contain significantly reduced or no active ingredient. Life-threatening risk of diabetic ketoacidosis. Cold-chain labeling present but non-functional.

Substandard dexamethasone injections with particulate contamination detected. Circulated widely during COVID-19 after dexamethasone was identified as an effective treatment for severe COVID-19. Risk of sepsis and emboli.
Substandard chloroquine products with highly variable active ingredient content (10–180% of stated dose). Risk of treatment failure and toxicity.
Falsified Fansidar tablets used in intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy. Contains no active ingredients. Risk of malaria in pregnant women and adverse birth outcomes.
Falsified artesunate injections detected in East Africa. Products used for severe malaria treatment. Contain subtherapeutic amounts of active ingredient. Potentially life-threatening.
Substandard amlodipine tablets with degraded active ingredient below 50% stated dose. Associated with uncontrolled hypertension in patients who switched to this product.

Falsified Lipitor (atorvastatin) tablets detected in Eastern Europe. Packaging nearly identical to genuine Pfizer product but hologram lacks rainbow shifting properties. Active ingredient content approximately 20% of stated dose.
Substandard diclofenac sodium injections with particulate contamination and pH outside acceptable range. Circulating in conflict zones where supply chain verification is difficult.
Substandard TB combination tablets with bioavailability failure. Hardness of tablets prevents adequate dissolution. Associated with TB treatment failure and emergence of drug resistance.

Falsified erythropoietin injections detected. Products contain saline or significantly reduced EPO. Used by anemia patients and (illicitly) in sports doping. Some batches contain immunogenic contaminants.
Substandard albendazole tablets used in mass drug administration for deworming programs. Active ingredient below 80% of stated amount, reducing effectiveness of public health deworming campaigns.

Falsified misoprostol tablets used for prevention of postpartum hemorrhage. Products contain minimal or no active ingredient. PPH is a leading cause of maternal mortality — falsified misoprostol is life-threatening.

Substandard epinephrine injections with significant degradation. Products exposed to excessive heat during transport, rendering the active ingredient ineffective. Risk of failed anaphylaxis treatment.

Systematic survey found over 60% of oxytocin products sampled in Sub-Saharan Africa failed quality standards. Poor cold-chain maintenance and substandard manufacturing leads to degraded active ingredient. Major contributor to postpartum hemorrhage deaths.
